text:
Ingrid: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A thread about engineering process (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). I'll summarize the decisions and answer the open questions here.

Lee: Appreciate it! Can you confirm the release cadence we're locking to? There was a lot of talk about faster shipping but also keeping quality.

Ingrid: Yep. Agreed on a predictable cadence:
```
- Major release train: every 2 weeks (Tue morning)
- Minor patches / non-breaking infra config: weekly (Thu)
- Emergency/hotfix: ad-hoc, follow rollback playbook
```
We expect feature rollouts to use the canary + staged percentage windows (see below).

Matt: For the 2-week train — are feature branches expected to land only before the code freeze? What does the freeze window look like?

Ingrid: Short answers: yes, land before greenline; freeze window is 48 hours before the Tue deploy for anything that touches runtime or model-serving infra. Non-critical UX work can be merged to trunk and toggled behind flags.

Sofia: On oncall: rotation length is 2 weeks, primary + secondary model. Escalation path: primary -> secondary -> oncall manager (pager duty escalation at 20m) -> SRE lead. A few specifics:
```
- Primary acknowledges within 10 min target (pager SLO)
- Primary tries mitigation or rollback within 30 min for infra/regression incidents
- If degraded SLA for hosted customers, follow incident runbook and notify CS within 1 hour
```

Matt: Is the 10 min ack required for Dedicated customers too? We get asked about response SLAs in sales.

Sofia: Same rota, but enterprise contracts can be configured with faster ack windows as part of the SLA add-on. Default internal pager SLO is 10 min. For Dedicated enterprise tiers we document contract-specific times in the customer's SOW.

Emily: On quality bars for model rollouts — what are the canary metrics and auto-rollback thresholds? I missed the detail in the deck.

Priya: Good question. Current policy we discussed:
- Canary population 5% for 1 hour, then 25% for 6 hours, then 100% if no regressions.
- Metrics monitored: generated quality (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or custom evals), token-error rate, latency p95/p99, and user-facing error rates.
- Auto-rollback triggers: any of the following during a canary window:
  - quality regression >5% on our labeled eval set
  - increase in user error rate >2x baseline
  - p99 latency increase >40% or p95 > 200ms over baseline for that model family
These are starting defaults and the ML team will tune per-model.

Lee: Where are the exact thresholds and playbooks stored? Ops needs a single source of truth for runbooks.

devbot: Release playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/release-cadence
Canary policy doc: https://redwood.internal/platform/canary-policy
Incident runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-response

Matt: A couple of sales asks: how do SLA credits work if we miss availability targets for hosted API? Can we point them to a public doc?

Ingrid: We have a public-facing SLA summary for hosted customers and more detailed contract language for enterprise. Summary: standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly uptime for API endpoints (see marketing SLA page); credits are pro-rata for downtime windows after investigation and confirmed incident classification. For Dedicated/private, SLA terms are in the customer contract. Linking internal summary: https://redwood.internal/sla-summary (sales-only).

Emily: For quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets — who owns the evals? Research or Product?

Priya: Shared ownership: Research manages the eval harness and model-side metrics, Product owns the prompt sets and acceptance criteria. Eng + SRE own the rollout automation. We'll publish a small org RACI in the playbook.

Lee: One last ops question — any change to the rollback authority? Can oncall revert without PM approval in emergencies?

Ingrid: Yes, rollback authority is delegated to oncall for incidents that meet the incident severity threshold (see runbook). PM/feature owners should be notified ASAP but not block a rollback.

Matt: Thanks. Is there an office hours/AMA for deeper stuff?

Ingrid: Yes — we'll run a 45-min office hours next Wed 4pm PT to walk the playbook and answer detailed questions. Add it to your calendars: https://calendar.internal/event/eng-playbook-qa. If you want pre-read, check the playbook links above.

Emily: Thanks — will review and flag follow-ups on the doc. :thumbsup:

Priya: I'll update the playbook with the canary numbers and RACI by EOD Friday.

Sofia: I'll post the oncall rota template and escalation contacts after the office hours.

Ingrid: Great — thanks everyone. If there's anything I missed tag me here and I'll add to the doc.
